note: The note game on the low E and A strings turned three ways: find and play the named note, say the lit note's name before pressing it, tap every place one note sits. One choice per level: beginner, intermediate and advanced up to fret 12 (note-finder level beginner, step notes-on-neck:2), and new up to fret 5 (note-finder level new, step notes-on-neck:1), the fret range a {{=fret}} param in the title. Folds in guitar-new-notes-on-e-and-a.

exercise.title: Notes on the low E and A strings, up to fret {{=fret}}
exercise.why: A chord shape or a scale position moved up the neck is named by the note under it on the low E or the A string, so knowing the notes on these two strings names every shape you move.

cells.text:
Press Playing it (mic) under the neck below. Then press Start above the neck.
The game names a note and a string: find it on your guitar and play it, saying its name out loud. The game hears your answer.
Practice until your finger goes to the note without counting frets up from the open string.

Press Start in the game below. Now the game lights a note on the neck: say its name out loud first, then press that name under the neck to check.
Play the note on your guitar as you answer, so your hand learns the place while your eyes learn the name.

Press Start in the game below. The game names a note: tap every place it sits on the two strings, then play those places on your guitar, low to high.
Notice which notes your finger goes to at once: the ones you still count up to are the ones to practice next.
